title: Anthropic Hits Nasdaq in Record $81B IPO as Global Markets Slip
description:
Anthropic makes history with a record-breaking $81 billion public debut on the Nasdaq. Meanwhile, global stock indexes face downside pressure, commodities slump, and European debt concerns weigh on sentiment.

Sources: Yahoo Finance, CNBC, MarketWatch, Investing.com, Marco Casario, Michael Pizzino, Jeremy Lefebvre

segments.heading: Anthropic Historic Nasdaq Debut
segments.narration: Anthropic makes history today with the largest initial public offering on record, raising $81 billion as shares begin trading on the Nasdaq. Meanwhile, global stock indexes face persistent selling pressure while European debt strain and falling commodity prices test investor sentiment.
bullets: Wall Street indexes face selling pressure

segments.heading: Market Briefing Today
segments.narration: Wall Street shows a mixed performance today following recent market volatility. The S&P 500 slipped 0.2% to 7,324 points, while the Dow Jones fell 1.1% to 50,198. Technology stocks offered relative support, driving the Nasdaq Composite up 0.4% to 24,430. Market volatility remains high, with the VIX settling at 25 points after dropping 3.5%. Fixed income markets stabilized slightly as the US 10-year yield dropped 0.7% to 5.1%. Foreign exchange markets saw EUR/USD decline 0.3% to 1.0965. Commodity prices posted steep losses across the board. Crude oil plunged 4.5% to $82.17 per barrel, and gold fell 3.6% to $3,727. In cryptocurrency markets, Bitcoin dropped 2.4% to $63,360, while Ethereum declined 1.4% to $1,797.

segments.heading: Anthropic Debut and Nvidia
segments.narration: Anthropic completed its historic public debut, pricing shares at $83 each. The offering raised over $81 billion, making it the largest initial public offering in market history as trading begins on the Nasdaq under ticker ANT. SEC filings detail total future compute infrastructure commitments near $518 billion, offset by $104 billion in operating losses over nine months during its rapid expansion phase. Investors are closely monitoring customer concentration risks and cash conversion cycles across major artificial intelligence developers. Concurrently, Nvidia leadership held its first employee town hall following record financial results. Nvidia posted fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, representing a year-over-year increase of more than 100%. Operating income hit $77.5 billion, yielding an operating margin near 67%. Nvidia continues to trade at approximately 10.8 times forward earnings, even as regulatory scrutiny and global supply chain commitments remain active factors in sector performance.
bullets: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 per share

segments.heading: Broad Equity Downtrend
segments.narration: Broader stock market benchmarks remain in a technical downtrend, with capital flowing defensively into the US dollar. Key overhead resistance for the S&P 500 stands firm near 7,600 points, while small-cap stocks have broken below prior support levels to trade near 2,890 points. Weak buying volume across broad index funds indicates that institutional capital is prioritizing risk reduction and cash preservation. Safe-haven demand for the US dollar continues to put downward pressure on foreign currencies and industrial commodities. Base metals and precious metals face persistent selling, with gold breaking lower after recent peaks. Energy markets reflect similar macroeconomic caution, with WTI crude oil experiencing strong monthly downside pressure. Account leverage across retail traders is contracting as market participants trim position sizes in high-multiple growth equities.
bullets: Small caps test lower support near 2,890

segments.heading: European Sovereign Debt Risks
segments.narration: European financial markets face growing concern over fiscal balances in the Eurozone. France carries a debt-to-GDP ratio of 119.1%, accompanied by negative third-quarter economic growth of -0.1%. Yields on ten-year French sovereign bonds reached 4.7%, surpassing Italy's 4.3% borrowing cost despite Italy holding a higher debt-to-GDP ratio of 139.9%. Foreign investors hold 57.5% of French national debt, heightening potential cross-border risk for European commercial banks. Fiscal requirements will force France to raise a record 340 billion euros in debt during 2027. European equity benchmarks reflected these fiscal tensions, as the FTSE MIB in Milan dropped 1.3% to 50,174 points and the Euro Stoxx 50 slipped 0.9% to 6,154. Eurozone assets remain sensitive to structural policy mechanisms designed to prevent sovereign spread fragmentation.

segments.heading: Palo Alto Expansion
segments.narration: In corporate earnings news, enterprise software and cybersecurity companies are demonstrating strong operational momentum. Palo Alto Networks announced a major $4.5 billion deal to acquire AI infrastructure provider Applied Compute while raising its full-year revenue outlook. Heightened global security demands and corporate investments in automated threat defense continue to drive expanding contract values. Corporate earnings prints show a widening divergence between cash-flow-generative software operators and capital-intensive hardware infrastructure providers. Companies tied directly to enterprise cloud migrations continue to report expanding order backlogs even as broader equity valuations compress.

segments.heading: Economic Calendar Outlook
segments.narration: Macroeconomic data will dictate market direction over the next several sessions. Today at 08:30 Eastern Time, the United States releases weekly Unemployment Claims, forecast at 198,000, alongside the Philly Fed Manufacturing Index, projected at 20.6. At the same time, European Central Bank President Lagarde delivers scheduled remarks. On Friday at 03:15 Eastern Time, President Lagarde speaks again ahead of the European market open. Later Friday at 10:00 Eastern Time, the University of Michigan releases revised Consumer Sentiment data, forecast at 51.7, alongside revised inflation expectations. Traders will scrutinize these economic prints for signals regarding future central bank interest rate policy.
